summary: Chile’s pledges mix sustainable native-forest management and recovery, afforestation and landscape restoration with protected-area and marine measures. Chile commits to managing or recovering 200,000 hectares of native forest and afforesting 200,000 hectares by 2030; each equals 2,000 km², about 0.84% of current forest cover, with respective annual carbon-capture goals of at least 0.9 and 3 MtCO2eq. It also plans to bring 1,000,000 hectares into restoration by 2030 (1.33% of national land area) and begin at least three water-security restoration plans by 2035, while expanding official continental terrestrial and aquatic protection by at least 1,000,000 hectares. Conservation targets include a 25% reduction in native-forest degradation and deforestation emissions by 2030, 20 new coastal wetlands by 2025 plus 10 more by 2030, and stronger planning, monitoring and adaptation across marine protected areas. Follow-on forest targets are 50,000 hectares under management and 25,000 hectares afforested during 2031–2035.
